paragraphs.title: The Command to Establish Cities of Refuge

easy.explanation: The first verse says that the Lord spake unto Joshua.
easy.q: To whom did the Lord speak at the beginning of the chapter?

easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Israel to appoint cities of refuge.
easy.q: What were the children of Israel commanded to appoint?

easy.explanation: The cities were a refuge from the avenger of blood.
easy.q: From whom were the cities of refuge to protect the slayer?

answers: To provide a place for an unintentional killer to flee
To allow a murderer to hide forever
To serve as homes for all the people
medium.explanation: The cities provided refuge for one who killed a person unintentionally.
medium.q: What was the purpose of the cities of refuge?

answers: The person who might pursue the slayer
medium.explanation: The slayer was to flee from the avenger of blood.
medium.q: In these verses, what does “the avenger of blood” refer to?

answers: He killed a person unawares and unwittingly
medium.explanation: The refuge was for someone who killed unintentionally and without knowing it.
medium.q: What condition describes the person who could flee to a city of refuge?

answers: The eligible person killed unintentionally, not out of hatred
The eligible person held an office in the city
challenge.explanation: The passage distinguishes an unintentional killing from an act motivated by hatred.
challenge.q: What was the main difference between the person eligible for refuge and someone who acted out of hatred?

answers: Protection is provided first, before the matter is judged
The person is judged first and flees afterward
The avenger of blood receives the person before the city does
challenge.explanation: The command first provides a place of refuge from the avenger of blood.
challenge.q: What can be learned from the order of events in these verses?

answers: To show that there was no intention to kill
To show that the person did not know the city
To show that the person was outside Israel
challenge.explanation: The wording makes clear that the killing was accidental rather than intentional.
challenge.q: Why is it emphasized that the killing was done “unawares and unwittingly”?

short_answers.question: Complete the phrase: “Appoint out for you cities of _____.”
short_answers.explanation: Joshua 20:2 commands Israel to appoint cities of refuge.

short_answers.question: What kind of person may flee to the city according to verse 3?
short_answers.answer: A slayer who killed a person unawares and unwittingly.
short_answers.explanation: Verse 3 describes the unintentional killer who may flee there.

short_answers.question: From whom do the cities provide refuge?
short_answers.explanation: The cities were appointed as protection from the avenger of blood.

paragraphs.title: Receiving the Fugitive and Bringing Him to Trial

answers: At the entering of the gate of the city
easy.explanation: The verse says that he stands at the entering of the city gate.
easy.q: Where does the slayer stand when he comes to the city?

easy.explanation: He declares his cause in the ears of the elders of that city.
easy.q: To whom does the slayer declare his cause?

answers: A place to dwell among them
easy.explanation: The elders take him into the city and give him a place to dwell among them.
easy.q: What do the elders give the slayer?

answers: Because he fled to another city
Because he killed unwittingly and had not hated his neighbour beforetime
Because he had already been judged
medium.explanation: The passage says that he smote his neighbour unwittingly and had not hated him beforetime.
medium.q: Why do the elders not deliver the slayer to the avenger of blood?

answers: Until he stands before the congregation for judgment and until the death of the high priest
Until the elders leave the city
Until the avenger of blood arrives
medium.explanation: He remains there until judgment and until the death of the high priest in those days.
medium.q: How long does the slayer remain in the city of refuge?

medium.explanation: The phrase means that the slayer had not hated the victim beforehand.
medium.q: What does “beforetime” mean in the phrase “hated him not beforetime”?

answers: He flees, dwells in the city, stands before the congregation, and then returns
He is judged, flees, receives a place, and then returns
He returns home, flees, is judged, and then receives a place
challenge.explanation: He flees to the city, is received there, faces judgment, and may return after the high priest’s death.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes what happens to the slayer?

answers: Permission from the avenger of blood
The death of the high priest who shall be in those days
The departure of the city elders
challenge.explanation: After the death of the high priest, the slayer may return to his own city and house.
challenge.q: What allows the slayer to return to his city and house?

answers: The circumstances are considered before he is received
The slayer does not need to stand trial
The elders decide to pursue him
challenge.explanation: He explains his case to the elders, and later stands before the congregation for judgment.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the fact that the slayer declares his cause to the elders?

short_answers.question: Where does the fugitive declare his cause?
short_answers.answer: In the ears of the elders of the city.
short_answers.explanation: He explains his case to the elders at the city gate.

short_answers.question: Until what two events does the slayer dwell in the city?
short_answers.answer: Until he stands before the congregation for judgment and until the death of the high priest.
short_answers.explanation: These two events mark the period of his stay.

short_answers.question: Where may the slayer go after the death of the high priest?
short_answers.answer: To his own city and his own house.
short_answers.explanation: The verse says he may return to the city from which he fled.

easy.explanation: The passage lists six cities of refuge.
easy.q: How many cities of refuge are listed in the chapter?

easy.explanation: Shechem was appointed in mount Ephraim.
easy.q: Which city was in mount Ephraim?

answers: For all the children of Israel and for the stranger sojourning among them
easy.explanation: The final verse includes both Israelites and resident foreigners among them.
easy.q: For whom were the cities appointed according to the final verse?

medium.explanation: Kedesh, Shechem, and Hebron were appointed in the land west of Jordan.
medium.q: Which group of three cities was west of Jordan in the land?

medium.explanation: Bezer was assigned out of the tribe of Reuben.
medium.q: Which city was assigned out of the tribe of Reuben?

answers: So they could flee there if they killed someone unintentionally
So they could serve as city elders
So they could choose the high priest
medium.explanation: The final verse includes the stranger who sojourned among Israel.
medium.q: Why were the cities also available to strangers dwelling among Israel?

challenge.explanation: The verse identifies Hebron as being in the mountain of Judah.
challenge.q: Which pairing of a city and its location is correct?

answers: The first three were in the land, and the last three were east of Jordan
The first three were in the wilderness, and the last three were in the mountains
The first three were for strangers, and the last three were for Israelites
challenge.explanation: The first three were in the land, while the other three were on the other side of Jordan.
challenge.q: What is the difference between the first three cities and the last three cities listed?

answers: To keep an unintentional killer from dying before standing before the congregation
To prevent anyone from leaving his city
To allow the avenger of blood to punish immediately
challenge.explanation: The cities protected an accidental killer until he could stand before the congregation.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of the cities according to the end of the chapter?

short_answers.question: Name the three cities appointed in the land west of Jordan.
short_answers.explanation: These are the first three cities listed in verse 7.

short_answers.question: Name the three cities appointed on the other side of Jordan.
short_answers.explanation: These cities are listed in verse 8.

short_answers.question: What was the slayer protected from until he stood before the congregation?
short_answers.answer: Being killed by the hand of the avenger of blood.
short_answers.explanation: The cities allowed him to flee and remain safe until judgment.
